selections.inspection_note: The inspected poster shows a blue-lit network switch populated with connected Ethernet cables and visible activity LEDs. It is a concrete infrastructure detail and does not claim to identify a particular facility.

The inspected poster shows operators working at a live multi-monitor control desk with operational displays visible around them. It reads as coordinated monitoring context, not as footage of the cited cyber incident.

The inspected poster shows one operator directly facing a wall of distinct live traffic and surveillance feeds. The human monitoring action is unambiguous while the displays remain generic operational context.

The inspected poster clearly shows rack-mounted server storage bays, visible SAS drive labels and illuminated status indicators. It depicts real computing infrastructure without identifying any institution in the story.

The inspected poster shows several operators in a wide control room following a large multi-feed wall display. It supplies an honest coordination-and-scale analogy rather than pretending to depict the cited espionage network.

The inspected poster shows a person presenting a hand or card at an active reader while entering through illuminated controlled turnstiles. It provides visible access-control context without presenting the location as a laboratory.

The inspected poster is a clear aerial view of one large industrial warehouse and its surrounding access roads. It communicates concentrated physical scale while remaining explicitly generic industrial context, not a claimed data centre.

The inspected poster clearly shows the exposed platter, actuator arm and head assembly of a mechanical hard disk in operation. It is an accurate component-level storage image and not a decorative device substitute.

The inspected poster shows a formal podium and panel setting with an unmistakable European Union flag. It is used only as generic governance context; legal obligations remain established by the primary evidence.

The inspected poster shows a technician physically examining a dense set of connected computer and network cables at a workstation. The action makes hardware maintenance tangible without acting as measurement evidence.

The inspected poster shows a central monitoring room with a large wall consolidating many distinct CCTV feeds and operators below it. It is a clear visual analogy for concentrated monitoring power, not evidence of the cited access policy.
